recipes.name: Rich Chocolate Truffle Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (9 inch) prepared chocolate cookie crumb crust

steps.text: Combine chocolate chips and 1/2 of the cream in a microwave-safe dish; cook on high for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring every 30 seconds until smooth. Cool to room temperature. Stir in sugar and vanilla. Set aside.
Beat remaining cream in a bowl with an electric mixer until soft peaks form.
Beat in chocolate mixture on high speed, 1/3 at a time.
Refrigerate for at least 8 hours before serving.
Slice and serve with a dollop of whipped cream.

raw_recipe.headline: Rich Chocolate Truffle Pie
raw_recipe.description: This no-bake chocolate truffle pie has a rich and luscious filling made with melted chocolate and cream poured into a chocolate cookie crust. Chill and serve to rave reviews!

video.description: Rich, quick, and delicious, this amazing chocolate pie has it all.

review.reviewBody: Easy Recipe to follow and make. I thought I could cheat and not let it chill for as long as the directions said...WRONG!!!! The flavor wasn't as intense as when it had chilled the 8 hours!!!! Delicious pie~

This recipe was amazing and so easy! I added 1 tsp instant coffee granules and it really enhanced the flavour! Also I made it in a springform pan and added fresh raspberries on top! It was a huge hit at our high end supper club where meals are second to none! I made it the day before and just added the whip cream, raspberries and a tiny sprinkle of shaved chocolate, just before serving! So impressive and no stress to put this together! Try it! You’ll be glad you did! ❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️

So good! I made it gluten free by making my own chocolate cookie crust (1 1/2 c gf chocolate cookie crumbs, 1 stick butter melted. Combine and press into pan, chill 15 mins, bake 10 mins at 350). I topped it with homemade whipped cream. It’s my family’s new favorite dessert.
very easy to make, tasty the second time I made it, I used 2 oz less chocolate chips and whipped the cream to stiff peaks before adding to the melted chips , made the pie have a lighter consistency

This was very easy to make and turned out well. I made it for some co-workers, who devoured the whole thing. The richness of the chocolate was fabulous. I chose to fold the whipped cream into the chocolate mixture instead of using a mixer to maintain the fluffiness and it worked perfectly. I used a pre-made cookie crust because it was so much easier and less time-consuming than trying to make one. I also recommend using a good quality semi-sweet chocolate for the best flavor.

I made an Oreo crust by mixing 2/3 pkg crushed Oreo's and 6 Tbls melted butter. I added 1/4 cup milk chocolate chips to the Ghirardelli semi-sweet chips and cream. After cooled, I added 1/3 c. Powdered sugar and a tablespoon of vanilla. I reserved 1/2 cup of Ganache then added the rest to the whipped cream. I then poured the Ganache into the bottom of the homemade chocolate crust , sprinkled crushed oreos, then the whip cream/chocolate mixture. Cooled completely. ..delicious.

Made the chocolate filling just as called for, but didn't have the chocolate crumb crust on hand. I made a crust using 3 tablespoons melted butter mixed with 20 smashed Oreo cookies and lined the bottom of an 8 X 8 baking dish. Poured in the filling and after refrigerating overnight, it was sinfully rich and delicious.

I am not a fan of chocolate cream pies, I don't really like pudding or chocolate mouse or anything like that very much, so I wanted to find something different. This looked perfect and I'm so glad I tried it. After reading most of the other reviewers, I took advice about making sure to wait for my chocolate mixture to cool completely to room temp and even give it a little longer after I thought it was ready. I noticed that many people liked the pie made with all semi-sweet chocolate chips while others preferred the milk chocolate, so I figured I should do half and half. Then I cut back on the sugar slightly and the vanilla just a tad. I also made sure to add the chocolate mixture to the heavy cream 1/3 at a time as directed. It came out heavenly. It was delicious alone but I whipped up some whipped cream for people to add if they wanted. I also put chocolate chips in top. Served it to the family at thanksgiving, everyone loved it! Even my brother who isn't the biggest chocolate fan. Perfect recipe, thanks for sharing!

made this last night for thanksgiving dinner today... i intended to only change the semisweet chips to milk chocolate... i used ghirdelli milk chocolate chips and added 1 oz of semi sweet chocolate chips... however while i was preparing it i was not focused and was doing a bunch of things at once and realized that something went wrong when the consistency was like soup... i know it was something i did wrong... did not whip the cream enough probably... so to fix it i added a box of chocolate pudding... added it to my premade cookie crust and hoped for the best... we had a small family dinner... just four of us... three adults and a child... my father didn't eat much and didn't want any desert... but between myself, my husband and my son we finished off half of this pie already... it was amazing... i can't say if it would have been better or worse without my mishap and need to add the pudding mix to thicken it up... but regardless... it was pie heaven!
The pie tasted very Chocolatey, but sadly the filling started to separate and get watery after all the chocolate mixture was beaten in. Would it be better to fold it in?

Clearly, something didn't work out. It was closer to fudge than a mousse. My chocoholic wife enjoyed it, but she's happy with dark chocolate chocolate chips. I think if I had folded the whipped cream in with the chocolate mixture, it probably wouldn't have killed the fluff. Still just tastes like melted semi-sweet chocolate to me. ROUND 2 RE-REVIEW: I can admit when I made a mistake. Make sure the chocolate mixture is completel cool. When you think it's been long enough, wait a little longer. If the chocolate mixture is warm at all, it will turn the whipped cream into liquid, and you will get fudge. If you are a hard core chocoholic, make this with bittersweet chocolate chips. Not for the faint of heart, but you will be a hero to those that can't find deserts chocolate-y enough for them.

Easy to make, tastes alright. Mainly just tastes like chocolate flavored whipped cream in a prepared crust. I guess that's what it is lol. For a real, rich pie taste, you need eggs, not just heavy cream.

Soooo easy to make!! My dad LOVED this pie and asked for it again! I am going to make it for Father's Day this weekend. I used a store bought graham cracker crust and also made my own graham cracker crust - both were a hit. Thank you!!
This makes a totally awesome desert for a special occasion or person.

I made this pie for Thanksgiving. Although I put a layer of chocolate truffle on top of a gluten-free crust. Possibly one of the finest chocolate cream pies I’ve ever made! Minimal ingredients for such an ahhmazing creation. I put 2/3 cup of heavy whipping cream in a pan to simmer. And then poured it over 6 ounces of semi sweet morsels. Whisk to a definite sheen. Pour on top of the crust and freeze for half an hour. I did not have to put any kind of whipped cream topping
Rich and velvety, with the perfect combo of crumbly crust and smooth chocolate filling. This pie is for true chocolate lovers.
Easy to make for sure. Very sweet and rich. One small piece is all you need unless you're a chocoholic sweet person. Everyone enjoyed it despite the sweetness. Will make again.
Simple to make and tastes delicious. My whole family loved it. I make it every Christmas!
If you like chocolate give this a try. Very easy to make and so delicious. The only thing I did different was to use a graham cracker crust instead of chocolate.
